newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Still no EU-South Africa trade deal.
newsitem.headline: Still no EU-South Africa trade deal.

text.p: The European Union and South Africa ended two days of trade talks in Brussels on Wednesday with "progress but no agreement", the European Commission said.
"We made progress on South Africa's partial accession to the Lome treaty and some on bilateral relations," a Commission spokesman said.

The spokesman said EU and South African trade negotiators had agreed broad terms for South Africa joining the Lome convention -- which governs EU relations with African, Caribbean and Pacific nations (ACP) -- and also a timetable for bilateral trade talks.
Partial Lome membership, the spokesman said, would give South Africa full political representation in the ACP but Pretoria would not be eligible for ACP development aid.
South Africa already receives over 125 million Ecus ($143 million) a year from the European Union in bilateral aid.
South Africa and the EU have been at odds over what kind of a trade deal to establish since Pretoria emerged from years of apartheid isolation.
